Definition: foreign, or (concretely) a foreigner, or (abstractly) heathendom
BiblicalUsage: No stranger shall eat of the passover, and the psalm commands that there shall be no strange god among God's people. Jacob tells his household to put away the strange gods that are among them, and Moses sings that the LORD alone led Israel, and there was no strange god with Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the strange god is the test of loyalty: the passover is closed to the stranger, the household must put its gods away, and the LORD alone leads His people, so I cannot keep a strange god beside Him and call Him Lord.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
